correctness.rationale: Euler's identity excludes common zeros of the two partial derivatives for a squarefree binary quartic, so the polar map has degree three. Its fiber over [s:t] is cut out by t f_X−s f_Y; the fixed target-coordinate change to the discriminant variables does not affect j. The three-root normalization covers all quartics in scope. Independently, in the even normal form X^4+z X²Y²+Y^4, the discriminant of the pencil with both partials divided by two is −8z³(u^4+v^4)+(z^4+72z²−432)u²v². Exact invariants give the asserted j-map; the branch discriminant in this family is 27648 z^6(z−6)^6(z−2)^2(z+2)^2(z+6)^6, vanishing precisely at J=0 among smooth inputs. The even normal form is available by conjugating a double-transposition involution of the four points to x↦−x and rescaling the two paired roots. The harmonic orbit is represented by X^4+Y^4, with cubic-power polar and branch divisor u²v². The two numerators for Φ and Φ−1728, plus the pole at infinity, give the listed partitions. Their defects sum to six, and a transitive subgroup of A4 containing a 3-cycle has order divisible by both four and three, hence equals A4. The affine change produces the classical level-three j-projection as a cover, not a modular polynomial relation involving the original quartic's own j.
residual_risks: The algebra is symbolic in characteristic zero. The pole at source j=∞ is a feature of the compactified rational map, not a claim about polars of singular quartics. No canonical isogeny involving the source quartic's elliptic curve is established.
